# Kotlin codegen for a list-typed var whose initializer is an expression
# rather than a literal: the expression must survive into the state
# declaration instead of being replaced by an empty list.

sngl generate --platform=android --lang=kotlin --out=out app.sngl
exists out/MainScreen.kt

# A list literal still becomes mutableStateListOf varargs.
grep 'val xs = remember \{ mutableStateListOf\(3, 1, 2\) \}' out/MainScreen.kt

# A non-literal list init keeps its expression, converted to snapshot state.
grep 'val rev = remember \{ xs\.reversed\(\)\.toMutableStateList\(\) \}' out/MainScreen.kt
grep 'val evens = remember \{ xs\.filter\(\{ n -> \(\(n % 2\) == 0\) \}\)\.toMutableStateList\(\) \}' out/MainScreen.kt

# An empty list is still typed explicitly, since Kotlin can't infer it.
grep 'val empty = remember \{ mutableStateListOf<Int>\(\) \}' out/MainScreen.kt

# Scalars are unaffected.
grep 'var idx by remember \{ mutableStateOf\(xs\.indexOf\(2\)\) \}' out/MainScreen.kt

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl://std"

output { kotlin { android } }

component main {
    var xs list<int> = [3, 1, 2]
    var rev list<int> = xs.reverse()
    var evens list<int> = xs.filter(func(n int) => n % 2 == 0)
    var empty list<int> = []
    var idx int = xs.indexOf(2)
    text(value=string(rev.length()) + string(evens.length()) + string(empty.length()) + string(idx))
}
